Given data: Number of poles ($P$) = $4$, Speed ($N$) = $1200\text{ rpm}$, Number of slots = $60$, Conductors per slot = $10$, Total conductors ($Z$) = $60 \times 10 = 600$, Flux per pole ($\Phi$) = $0.03\text{ Wb}$, Armature winding = Lap wound (so number of parallel paths $A = P = 4$).

The induced e.m.f. in a DC generator is given by the EMF equation:
$$E = \frac{\Phi \cdot Z \cdot N \cdot P}{60 \cdot A}$|

Since for lap winding $A = P$, the formula simplifies to:
$$E = \frac{\Phi \cdot Z \cdot N}{60}$$

Substituting the values:
$$E = \frac{0.03 \times 600 \times 1200}{60}$$
$$E = 0.03 \times 600 \times 20 = 360\text{ V}$$

**Answer:** The induced e.m.f. in the armature is **$360\text{ V}$**.
proTip: For lap-wound generators, number of parallel paths ($A$) equals the number of poles ($P$). For wave-wound, $A = 2$. Always double-check your winding type.
